projects.name: Nairagram
projects.headline: Engineering the systems behind cross-border money movement.
projects.summary: Platform ownership across consumer remittance, business payments, partner APIs, payout operations, compliance, and reconciliation.
projects.context: A cross-border payment ecosystem needs more than a working transfer screen. It needs dependable coordination between customers, payment gateways, payout partners, compliance teams, finance, and day-to-day operations. My role connects those parts through architecture, engineering leadership, and hands-on production work.
contributions: Own engineering strategy, platform architecture, technical roadmap, delivery governance, and production reliability across C2C, B2C, B2B, and administrative platforms.
Work across 10+ pay-in gateway/API/SDK integrations and 50+ payout partner APIs, covering authentication, onboarding, transaction submission, status callbacks, and operational issue resolution.
Strengthen transaction lifecycle control with traceable status histories, webhook handling, retry controls, exception management, reconciliation workflows, and payout recovery.
Build and improve ID verification, fraud detection support, transaction monitoring, access controls, API protection, and audit trails.
Develop Python-based forecasting with Prophet, XGBoost, and LightGBM, alongside BigQuery-backed analytics and operational reporting.
Lead cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, release controls, database performance work, monitoring, and incident response while partnering with product, finance, compliance, and operations.
outcomes: Supported more than $1B in cross-border payment volume.
Scaled the engineering function from 5 to 20 members.
Connected platform delivery with the operational needs of a growing payment ecosystem.
projects.lesson: A payment is only complete when the platform can explain its state, its money movement, and the evidence behind both.

projects.name: Nairagram Basket
projects.headline: A partner API platform with operational visibility built in.
projects.summary: A partner-facing payment API and dashboard connecting business integrations with transaction monitoring and operational control.
projects.context: Business partners need a consistent integration surface and a clear view of the transfers they initiate. Nairagram Basket brings API access, payment workflows, and partner visibility together in a dedicated B2B platform.
contributions: Design and improve partner API workflows for initiating payments, checking status, and receiving transaction updates.
Build partner dashboard capabilities for transaction tracking, investigation, and day-to-day integration support.
Support controlled partner access, API authentication, onboarding, and integration troubleshooting.
Connect partner activity with payout orchestration, administrative operations, and reconciliation processes.
Improve error handling, callback processing, and traceability across external partner and internal payment workflows.
outcomes: A dedicated integration channel for business partners.
Better visibility from API submission through payout status and operational follow-up.
projects.lesson: A useful partner API is supported by clear state, actionable errors, and a dashboard that helps people solve real cases.

projects.name: Ping Express / PingBasket
projects.headline: From payment journeys to disciplined engineering delivery.
projects.summary: Cross-border remittance engineering spanning B2C/B2B flows, exchange rates, payout integrations, mobile APIs, and operational tools.
projects.context: A remittance product has to join the customer journey with exchange-rate logic, compliance handling, payout processing, and support operations. I led development planning and hands-on engineering across these workflows while strengthening how the team shipped and supported changes.
contributions: Lead cross-functional development planning, technical task allocation, code review, milestone delivery, and production stabilization.
Architect sender and receiver workflows, currency exchange logic, payout integrations, compliance handling, and transaction tracking.
Build and support API layers consumed by web clients, mobile applications, and business partners.
Improve operational tools for payment teams, including status visibility, reconciliation support, and investigation of failed transactions.
Strengthen testing discipline, review practices, release checks, and hands-on mentoring.
outcomes: Reduced post-production defects by 90% through stronger reviews, testing practices, and mentoring, as recorded in my professional résumé.
Built a foundation in connecting engineering quality to payment reliability.
projects.lesson: Release discipline is a product capability when software is responsible for moving customers’ money.

projects.name: MasterRemit
projects.headline: Improving an established remittance backend with care.
projects.summary: Code review, backend upgrades, API improvements, and production support for an Australia-based payment platform.
projects.role: Backend Engineering / Code Review / Upgrade Support
projects.context: An established payment platform must keep serving customers while its code, integrations, and application interfaces evolve. My contribution focused on reviewing backend code, supporting upgrades, and improving the maintainability and behavior of existing systems.
contributions: Review developer code and support platform upgrades across existing mobile and C2C applications.
Work on CodeIgniter backend services, payment-related fixes, and application maintenance.
Improve API behavior and integration reliability for mobile and web consumers.
Investigate transaction-flow defects and assist with production issues.
Support practical modernization while respecting the needs of an operating remittance business.
outcomes: Focused improvements to existing payment systems and application integrations.
Hands-on experience upgrading business-critical fintech software.
projects.lesson: Good modernization starts with understanding what the existing platform already has to protect.

projects.name: PingMoney
projects.headline: Connecting the frontend, payment APIs, and partner network.
projects.summary: Laravel APIs and Angular integration for pay-in, payout, transaction flows, and web/mobile fintech experiences.
projects.context: PingMoney combines a customer-facing Angular application with Laravel backend APIs and external payment providers. My work centered on improving how those layers communicate and how transactions behave through the payment lifecycle.
contributions: Support Laravel backend APIs consumed by frontend and mobile applications.
Integrate and maintain pay-in and payout gateway connections and partner APIs.
Improve transaction-processing workflows, API responses, and integration error handling.
Support partner communication, production troubleshooting, and payment-flow issue resolution.
Contribute across B2B/C2C platform capabilities and ongoing product development.
outcomes: Stronger integration between customer experiences and payment-provider workflows.
Practical full-stack support across a market-specific fintech platform.
projects.lesson: Integration quality is visible to customers even when the complexity stays behind the API.

projects.name: ROOO
projects.headline: Real-time dispatch meets payment-grade backend control.
projects.summary: Rider, driver, and admin APIs connecting dispatch, live location, scheduled rides, notifications, wallets, and payments.
projects.context: A ride-hailing backend coordinates changing driver availability, location, booking state, notification delivery, and payment outcomes. My work brings these moving parts into a controlled ride lifecycle for rider, driver, and administrative applications.
contributions: Build modular Laravel controllers, services, queued jobs, and backend APIs for instant bookings, scheduled rides, and opportunity-based ride flows.
Implement driver assignment using availability checks, distance filters, round-robin selection, cooldown rules, reassignment, and offline-driver safeguards.
Support scheduled ride reminders, pre-start checks, notification windows, and controlled ride-state transitions.
Integrate MQTT messaging and Firebase FCM fallback with retries, deduplication, and stale-token handling.
Build Stripe payment workflows, wallet debit/credit handling, invoicing, dynamic fare rules, stop charges, and cancellation logic.
Implement route snapping, distance calculations, ETA logic, location tracking, and Google Maps/Mapbox switching.
outcomes: A connected backend across dispatch, geospatial decisions, customer communication, and financial workflows.
Reusable orchestration and helper layers for complex ride operations.
projects.lesson: Real-time software still needs deliberate state transitions. Fast messages cannot compensate for ambiguous business rules.

projects.name: AmitBookDepot
projects.headline: An online bookstore connected to the work behind the counter.
projects.summary: Commerce and Laravel ERP covering stock, POS, invoices, payroll, attendance, customer records, and communication.
projects.context: Book retail has operational needs that a basic online catalog does not cover. The platform combines an online bookstore with a custom ERP for stock, billing, people, and customer operations, including business rules specific to books and institutional retail.
contributions: Build e-commerce capabilities for books, stationery, academic products, and related retail categories.
Develop attendance, payroll, overtime calculation, and operational reporting modules.
Implement inventory management, invoice generation, POS billing, customer/student records, and categorization.
Model bookstore-specific stock, billing, and rental business rules.
Connect email, SMS, and WhatsApp communication workflows for customer engagement and operations.
outcomes: Connected storefront and back-office workflows in a purpose-built operational platform.
Reduced fragmentation across inventory, billing, staff, and customer information.
projects.lesson: The most useful business software reflects the details of how that business actually works.

projects.name: MarineIMS / IMS X7
projects.headline: One learning platform. Many institutes. Clear boundaries.
projects.summary: Multi-role LMS and institute management with tenant subdomains, academic operations, fee payments, and online learning.
projects.context: An institute management system needs to serve administrators, teachers, students, and multiple institutions while keeping responsibilities and information clearly separated. MarineIMS combines academic administration with online learning and fee management.
contributions: Build role-based administrator, institute, teacher, and student workflows.
Support multi-institute operation through separate wildcard subdomains.
Implement attendance, classes, courses, assignments, exams, enrollment, and student lifecycle capabilities.
Connect course-fee payment workflows with institute operations.
Integrate online learning tools including Webex, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, and digital whiteboard support.
outcomes: A shared platform supporting distinct institute operations.
Connected academic administration, learning delivery, and payments.
projects.lesson: Multi-tenancy is an operating model as much as it is a database and routing decision.

projects.name: Canadian Real-Estate Data
projects.headline: Turning external property feeds into useful discovery.
projects.summary: Third-party listing ingestion, structured property data, search, filtering, and refresh workflows for a Canadian real-estate use case.
projects.context: Property discovery depends on current, structured data and useful search. My contribution focused on bringing third-party listing information into an application, organizing it consistently, and making it easier for customers to find relevant properties.
contributions: Fetch and normalize third-party listing data for a Canadian real-estate application.
Work with REALTOR.ca-related listing data and integration workflows.
Build search and filtering behavior around structured property attributes.
Support listing refreshes and live or near-real-time update workflows.
Improve how property information is presented to users.
outcomes: External data transformed into a searchable property experience.
A foundation for keeping listing discovery aligned with refreshed source data.
projects.lesson: An API feed becomes a product only when its data is consistent, current, and understandable.

projects.name: Multicurrency Ledger & Revenue
projects.headline: Accounting for every movement across currencies and partners.
projects.summary: Double-entry ledger design, wallet and partner positions, reconciliation, FX handling, and CAD-based revenue reporting.
projects.context: A customer wallet balance and the actual position at a bank or payout partner describe different parts of the same financial system. This work separates those positions and makes credits, debits, funding, payouts, and revenue calculations explainable through a ledger and supporting reports. Details here describe architecture and test-environment work, rather than a production-launch claim.
contributions: Design double-entry posting flows for wallet funding, customer debits, payout execution, and payout-partner prefunding.
Separate customer liabilities from bank, clearing, and partner liquidity positions across currencies.
Define idempotent posting, atomic database transactions, currency validation, reversal controls, and append-only financial records.
Model reconciliation against provider statements and operational follow-up for unresolved differences.
Design FX and revenue calculations with CAD reporting, explicit rate references, fixed-precision amounts, and traceable cost components.
Create administrative views for ledger balances, revenue detail, and currency-pool monitoring.
outcomes: A concrete implementation model linking money movement, ledger postings, reconciliation, and revenue reporting.
Schema, sample-data, and interface designs for test-environment implementation.
projects.lesson: A dashboard total should be the end of an explainable accounting trail, not the start of a guessing exercise.

projects.name: Stellar Remittance Prototype
projects.headline: Connecting familiar remittance flows with on-chain settlement.
projects.summary: Stellar/Soroban testnet work across funding verification and crypto-to-fiat, fiat-to-crypto, and crypto-to-crypto API flows.
projects.context: A blockchain rail still has to fit into a complete payment product: customer flows, funding confirmation, provider APIs, payout handling, and operational evidence. This engagement explores those connections in a prototype and testnet setting.
contributions: Connect Stellar funding and payout workflows to application APIs.
Implement funding verification using Horizon evidence and testnet payment checks.
Work on endpoint flows for crypto-to-fiat, fiat-to-crypto, and crypto-to-crypto journeys.
Organize provider integration modules and backend orchestration for payment workflows.
Contribute to integration planning around customer registration, KYC, funding, and settlement.
outcomes: Successful testnet payment and funding-verification checks.
Backend integration work connecting on-chain events with application payment flows.
projects.lesson: On-chain confirmation is one part of settlement. A usable product must also explain provider state, customer state, and the off-chain outcome.

projects.name: Payment Operations Control Layer
projects.headline: Making complex payment operations easier to see and control.
projects.summary: Prototype engineering around payment orchestration, payout networks, workflow boundaries, reconciliation, and operational visibility.
projects.context: Payment businesses often operate across multiple providers, application boundaries, and operational teams. This work focuses on a control layer that helps connect those pieces through defined workflows, integration boundaries, and evidence-driven testing. The portfolio describes prototype and architecture contributions.
contributions: Contribute to architecture and delivery of an operational control-layer prototype for payment workflows.
Work on payout-network integration boundaries, API behavior, and web/worker coordination.
Support workflow remediation, security boundaries, and automated acceptance checks.
Connect transaction status and reconciliation concepts with operational visibility.
Translate product and stakeholder needs into engineering scope and implementation priorities.
outcomes: Prototype workflows and integration boundaries supported by automated verification.
A practical foundation for conversations across product, operations, and engineering.
projects.lesson: A control layer earns its place by making the underlying systems easier to operate and explain.
